title: BARQ: Boundary-Aware Regularized Training for Accurate Inference on Computing-in-Memory Accelerators with Low-Precision A/D Conversion
problem: Computing-in-Memory (CIM) accelerators using low-precision ADCs suffer from quantization-induced errors that degrade inference accuracy. Traditional quantization methods cannot maintain accuracy when ADC bit-width is reduced to 3 bits or lower.
motivation: Lowering ADC precision reduces system area and power but increases numerical errors—achieving this trade-off requires novel training techniques.
method: BARQ adds constraints during training that keep numeric values within the range of the low-precision converter, preventing overflow and clipping errors where values get cut off. It uses a mathematical technique (Euclidean projection) to initialize the model's weights in a way that minimizes quantization error from the beginning. This approach also makes weights sparse (randomly setting some to zero), which reduces computation and helps training converge faster and more reliably.
key_novelty: The core innovation is adding constraints during training based on the low-precision converter's boundary limits to prevent overflow errors during inference.
contributions: ADC bit-width boundary constraints for regulated weight quantization during training
Euclidean projection-based weight initialization for reduced initial quantization error
Up to 75% energy reduction and 3.79× hardware efficiency improvement through enhanced sparsity
Minimal 0.59% accuracy loss on CIFAR-10/100/ImageNet even with 3-bit ADCs
limitations: Analysis limited to convolutional neural networks; applicability to other DNN architectures not discussed.
